lineage.canonicalPublicDirection:
Use case: stylized-concept
Asset type: Sable Reach environment-direction keyframe for Hearthmere Wave 03C
Input images: Image 1 is the accepted Hearthmere regional keyframe, used only for its cold rainy blue-gray atmosphere, wet-slate and repaired-dark-timber material language, restrained oxblood cloth, scarce ember warmth, hand-built density, and grounded stylized 3D dark-fantasy finish. Do not copy or preserve its lake, coast, cliffs, mountains, central monolith, banners, exact building arrangement, camera, or implied geography.

Primary request: Create a new polished stylized 3D dark-fantasy production concept of Hearthmere’s inhabited civic spring spine. It must make the current playable prototype’s anchor relationship recognizable while remaining explicitly an illustrative direction image rather than canonical geometry.

Format and camera: 1536×1024 landscape. Human third-person eye height, approximately 1.65 meters above the route, with a natural 28–32 mm equivalent lens and only a slight downward pitch. Place the conceptual camera near the current prototype player-start relationship and face generally east: Hearthmere Square is immediately forward and slightly right; the single timber bell tower is ahead-left/northeast; the single spring-channel arch is ahead-right/southeast. Do not show coordinates, a map, a diagram, or an aerial plan.

Exact landmark counts: Show exactly ONE dominant splinted timber civic bell tower, exactly ONE open public square, and exactly ONE stone spring-channel arch. Do not add a second tower, second belfry, second spring arch, second plaza, monumental statue, carved monolith, cathedral, castle keep, or duplicate landmark. The tower should dominate the local silhouette through height and timber lattice, but the image must not claim or display an exact measurement.

Route composition: Show exactly THREE clearly different traversal roles in one continuous scene:
1. a broad primary wet-slate public route entering the open square;
2. a narrower risk-and-service route following the spring channel, usable by water carriers and a handcart;
3. a distinct return/shortcut lane passing inhabited thresholds and reconnecting toward the camera side.
The three routes must be visually traceable, must not collapse into one indistinct courtyard, and must retain believable walking surfaces, stair rises, landings, edge protection where needed, ordinary doors, cart turns, and unobstructed egress. Do not draw route lines or use colored wayfinding overlays.

Water and drainage: Hearth Spring is a real warm spring, not magic light, lava, blackwater, or a decorative canal. Show clear directional downhill flow through an open stone-lined rill and beneath the single spring-channel arch, with subtle low steam and warm reflected light. Keep the drinking/service spring visually separate from roof runoff. Steep slate roofs shed cold rain into gutters, rain chains, iron-bound barrels, and shallow maintained drainage rills; runoff must not pour across the public route, flood door thresholds, or fall directly into the spring source. Show plausible repair access to the channel without claiming hydraulic capacity or engineering validity.

Architecture: Use human-scale one- and two-story slate tenant houses with repaired black-pine cruck frames, steep mismatched slate roofs, patched lime, rain-dark lower courses, visible timber splints, soot fans above shared hearths, and doorframes preserving earlier tenant heights. Include the grounded slate base and timber language of Hearthmere’s bell-and-ledger civic house. A broad-roof washed-slate hospice mass may appear in the background as proposal-only typology, with controlled rain-court drainage and no sacred-white cleanliness; its exact placement is not fixed. A repaired palisade may close the distant settlement edge, but it must read as survival carpentry rather than a military castle.

Materials and light: Preserve the Hearthmere palette hierarchy: near-black shadow approximately #0b1113; rain-dark stone approximately #424b4c; repaired timber approximately #332a24; restrained oxblood cloth approximately #683f37; scarce civic ember/bronze approximately #c18b46; cold fog approximately #829492. Use cold overcast raking light, wet-slate reflections, subtle warm-spring bounce, and small banked-brazier practicals. Warm light must remain localized and accountable to work, shelter, or civic service. No broad golden sunset, heroic sunbeam, neon magic, excessive bloom, clean white marble, or glossy fantasy metal.

Inhabited evidence and player scale: The hold must feel maintained and occupied, not abandoned. Show six to nine ordinary noncombat residents performing different tasks: ledger work, lamp maintenance, water carrying, handcart movement, hospice delivery, market repair, herb handling, or roof-drain maintenance. Use ordinary door heights, residents, handrails, benches, barrels, carts, stairs, tools, and threshold wear as scale evidence. Include one public Ember Ledger work station at the square edge, one clay-name rack with tablets whose markings are completely unreadable, one chained stone spring cup, banked braziers, at least one iron-bound rain barrel, a patched market awning, a traveler bench, a herb-drying frame, and a guard weapon rest. These objects must occupy credible working locations rather than appear as a prop lineup.

Environmental history: Make three time layers readable without labels: the old settlement’s slate and spring infrastructure; materially different survival repairs in black pine, mismatched slate, patched lime, and cloth; current civic pressure visible through queues, maintenance, ration work, lamp service, and guarded but open thresholds. Repairs remain additive and do not erase prior damage. The square center stays traversable and contains no statue or monolith.

Surroundings: Hearthmere is a Graven March slate-upland spring settlement. Use black-pine silhouettes, a cairn ridge, ash-filtered drizzle or sleet, low fog, and cold resinous air as distant environmental cues. Do not depict an ocean, harbor, beach, fjord, huge lake, sea cliffs, coastal islands, alpine citadel, or vast mountain amphitheatre. Do not imply that Hearthmere is a seaport.

Creatures and factions: This is the ordinary civic baseline. Show no active enemy, angelic being, demon, giant supernatural body, faction procession, battle, corpse display, or creature encounter. Residents must not read as duplicated anonymous soldiers, worshippers, or a ceremonial crowd. No heraldic shorthand.

Forbidden content: No text, letters, numerals, readable tablet marks, signs, labels, captions, map, compass, arrows, route lines, color-coded diagram, inset, cutaway, split screen, UI, HUD, logo, watermark, presentation border, concept-art callout, rune, readable insignia, monumental monolith, generic Gothic cathedral, castle battlements, purposeless spikes, floating debris, impossible stairs, decorative machinery, or unexplained monumental scale.

Review boundary and nonclaims: This image is environment and player-scale direction only. It must not claim exact atlas or GIS placement, cadastral boundary, surveyed coordinate transfer, exact dimensions, final site topology, final room adjacency, hydrology performance or capacity, structural or construction validity, accessibility or fire-code compliance, collision, navigation, encounter layout, streaming, lighting or VFX implementation, runtime integration, static or animated model readiness, production geometry, or production-asset status. The tracked 96×96 meter prototype anchor relationship informs the composition, but the image does not redefine that runtime scene or establish the larger 192-meter core and 640-meter influence envelope as exact visible boundaries.
